comments.author: Raju Dandigam
comments.comment: The layer I see teams underbuild is evals: a 95% retrieval hit rate can still fail if the retrieved chunk is stale, contradictory, or missing the action constraint. I like separating evals into retrieval quality, tool-call correctness, and final-answer behavior, because one aggregate score hides the real failure mode. Which layer breaks first for you once real users start asking messy questions?

comments.author: DAIR.AI
comments.comment: The useful split is agent capability vs agent trust. A model can look better on pass@k while getting worse in production because retries hide bad planning, extra tool calls, and higher latency. What eval would you trust most for agents: final answer accuracy, per-step verification, or cost-adjusted success rate?

comments.author: Daniel Bertram
comments.comment:
The underrated part of agent workflows is not the model choice, it is the boundary design.

A folder structure is really a memory and permissions system in disguise: what the agent can see, where drafts land, what gets reviewed, and what never gets touched automatically.

I would keep one manual approval gate until the failure modes are boring.

comments.author: Marc Baumann
comments.comment: I’d add an eval and rollback layer across the whole stack. Once agents own recurring workflows, the hard part stops being model choice and becomes drift detection: golden task sets, cost/latency budgets, human escalation thresholds, and a clean way to replay failures. Are you versioning skills and prompts the same way you version code?

comments.author: Giels Brouwer
comments.comment: The hard part is not cloning the visible workflow, it is preserving the invisible contract: edge cases, permissions, failure states, latency budgets, and data semantics. Reverse engineering can get you to a convincing demo fast, but production quality still comes from evals that compare behavior across hundreds of messy user paths. My question is: will teams use this to learn faster, or just ship more lookalikes with worse reliability?
